newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bank CCB eyes tie-up with SMAP/OMOB.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bank CCB eyes tie-up with SMAP/OMOB.

text.p: Belgium's second largest bank Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB), which is about to link up with Credit Local de France, said on Monday it is also investigating a possible tie-up with SMAP/OMOB, Belgium's third largest insurance company.

"There's no plan at the moment...but if something happens it would be to make a bancassurance group. It's clear that at the level of CCB an alliance with SMAP/OMOB would be within this context," CCB chief executive officer Francois Narmon told a news conference.
CCB also controls Luxembourg's Banque Internationale.
Narmon was speaking after CCB shareholders -- Belgium's towns and municipalities -- overwhelmingly approved the alliance with CLF.
Under the terms of the alliance CCB will sell between 25 and 30 percent of its shares to institutional and retail investors through an initial public offering on the Brussels Stock Exchange.
SMAP/OMOB could acquire a stake in CCB as part of this process, Narmon said. But he denied weekend newspaper reports that there was an agreement SMAP/OMOB would take a five percent interest.
"There are two problems that have to be cleared. One is when the SMAP accord can be finalised...the second is the size of the stake," Narmon said.
He said CCB was still investigating whether SMAP/OMOB could enter into the capital of CCB Holding -- the name of the company that will be listed -- before a prospectus on the sale had been issued.
If this was the case, the size of the overall allocation to institutional investors and the general public would be correspondingly diminished, he said.
